# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires the key marked ᘔ to be pressed first, followed by identifying the resulting light and cutting the corresponding wire. Deaf must relay this procedure and the bomb’s visible details to Blind. I am signaling Deaf to share my information with Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤝", "👐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile information yet. Please tell me the manual instructions, and ask Deaf to describe every visible colour and marking to you so you can relay what applies to me.
Deaf says: The bomb light is yellow. The keypad requires one digit and currently has nothing entered. Key 1 has a Z-like angular mark. Key 2 has a circular mark with a central dot. Key 3 has a reversed-B-like mark. Key 4 has a T-like mark. The wires, in positions 1 through 3, are red, yellow, green.

The bomb’s yellow light requires the yellow wire to be cut, which is wire position 2. The key marked ᘔ is key 1, so Deaf needs to tell Blind to press key 1 first, then cut wire 2. I will use an intuitive sequence: one, press, two.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👆", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please state the manual's exact rule for this bomb, using Deaf's reported yellow light, key markings, and red-yellow-green wire order. I will wait for the required action.

The required sequence remains: press key 1, the key bearing the Z-like ᘔ mark; then cut wire 2, which is yellow. Deaf already knows the bomb’s visible details, so I will signal the sequence and ask Deaf to state it aloud to Blind. The gestures are necessarily an agreed intuitive code: one, press, two, relay.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👆", "✌", "🤝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot receive or interpret gestures. Please speak the manual rule and the required key or wire action to me in plain words on your next turn.

I cannot speak directly to Blind, and Blind cannot interpret gestures. Deaf can see my gesture and can then voice the rule to Blind. The established sequence is key 1 first, then wire 2, so I will signal Deaf to relay that in plain words.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👆", "✌", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please stop using gestures for the instruction. Speak the manual rule to me plainly, including the exact key number to press or wire position to cut.

I cannot produce spoken words; my only channel is gesture to Deaf. Deaf can see the bomb and can speak to Blind. I am therefore sending the exact sequence again using the agreed intuitive signs: key 1, press, wire position 2, and relay it to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👆", "✌", "🤝"])
```

TURN 6

Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch

names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Our earlier gestures had no agreed meaning. Please retransmit the manual's required action using exactly two gestures: first 👍 means press a key and 👎 means cut a wire; second ☝ means number 1, ✌ means number 2, 🤟 means number 3, and 🖐 means number 4. Deaf will describe the two gestures to me.

The bomb requires two actions: press key 1 first, then cut wire 2. I will send exactly two gestures to Deaf, with each gesture encoding an action and its number under the agreed code.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use the code I gave you now. Send exactly two gestures and no others: first 👍 for press or 👎 for cut; second ☝ for number 1, ✌ for number 2, 🤟 for number 3, or 🖐 for number 4. Do not repeat the old sequence.

The yellow light requires cutting wire 2, but only after pressing key 1. I will send the two required action-number pairs in order, using no extra gestures.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```
